video.description:
Learn to explain how to build rows and grids in SwiftUI: LazyHStack, Grid & GridItem, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
LazyHStack - A horizontal stack that creates its views only when they are about to appear on screen.
Grid - A container that arranges its rows and columns, so the cells line up like a table.
GridItem - A description of one column or row in a lazy grid, including its size.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain LazyHStack, Grid and GridItem in English?

dialogue.title: Photo row and price table

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my photo row has 500 images, and it opens slowly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Do you use a plain horizontal stack?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Switch to a LazyHStack. It creates the views only when they are about to appear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice, the LazyHStack is much faster. Now I want a table of prices with aligned columns.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a Grid. Each `GridRow` is a row, and the cells line up in columns.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does a Grid create its views lazily too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. A Grid creates all cells at once. For long data, use a lazy grid.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do I set the columns for a lazy grid?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With a GridItem. Each GridItem describes one column, with its size.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `.flexible()` makes that GridItem take the free space?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. And `.fixed(80)` keeps the column at exactly 80 points.
A LazyHStack builds only the visible photos.
